'''Billy Dexter''' is the host of ''[[Entertaining America]]'' on [[West Coast Talk Radio (3D Universe)|WCTR]] in ''[[Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas]]''.

He is voiced by [[Peter Marx]].

==History==
===Events of ''Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas''===
In [[1992]] he had wanted to call the show ''Stack the Dex'', but was unable to change the name. He interviewed [[Jack Howitzer (3D Universe)|Jack Howitzer]] on his show, and later planned to interview French chef [[Richard Goblin]].

During his interview with Howitzer, they play the trailer for his upcoming film ''[[Special Needs Cop]]'', only to be completely disgusted by the insenstive content. He then claims that Howitzer is out of touch and that things are more sensitive in 1992. This angers Howitzer, who threatens him with a submachine gun. Howitzer then forces Billy to touch his genitalia to dispel a previous accusation Billy made, that steroids have shrunk his genitals, before fatally and accidentally shooting him in the head with the gun (which he thought wasn't loaded).

Howitzer is later put on trial for the murder of Dexter, who was later replaced by [[Lazlow Jones (3D Universe)|Lazlow Jones]] as the new host of ''Entertaining America''.

He is evidently a follower of the [[Epsilon Program (3D Universe)|Epsilon Program]] as he can frequently be heard saying the name of the cult's supposed celestial deity, Kifflom.

===HD Universe===
In ''[[Grand Theft Auto V]]'', a Weazel News report<!---News #90 on "All GTA V Weazel News Reports" on YouTube. File reference to be added.---> mentions an incident in the early 1990s, in which [[Jack Howitzer (HD Universe)|Jack Howitzer]] accidentally killed an unidentified radio host. This is a reference to the previous incarnation of [[Jack Howitzer (3D Universe)|Jack Howitzer]]'s character in the [[3D Universe]] accidentally shooting Billy Dexter. However, Dexter is not mentioned by name and this event happened in a different continuity of the series.

Dexter is one of the honored celebrities on the [[Vinewood Walk of Fame]].
